summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 establishes a human-centered federal framework for artificial intelligence in education and the workforce. The bill sets up grant programs, interagency councils, and strategic planning initiatives to promote ethical artificial intelligence teaching and learning, support workforce reskilling and apprenticeships, protect data privacy, address environmental impacts of artificial intelligence infrastructure, and ensure equitable access for underserved communities.

affected_groups.effect: Receive enhanced AI literacy curricula, data privacy protections, opt-out mechanisms for AI tools, and specialized teacher and school leader training, while minority-serving institutions gain capacity-building grants.
Gain access to AI reskilling programs, apprenticeships, and career equity initiatives, alongside protections against fully automated employment decisions.
Can apply for an artificial intelligence reskilling tax credit, receive guidance on AI use in hiring and performance evaluations, and must follow compliance requirements if receiving federal funds.
Receive environmental disclosures regarding water and energy consumption of data centers, alongside grants for local oversight and environmental monitoring.

key_provisions: Establishes a list of artificial intelligence-augmented occupations and an Interagency Council on Artificial Intelligence in Education and the Workforce to coordinate federal activities and strategies.
Creates grant programs for artificial intelligence-disrupted career pathways, stackable micro-credentials, and equitable access in elementary, secondary, and postsecondary education.
Authorizes a National Artificial Intelligence Workforce Strategy and grant programs for apprenticeships, pre-apprenticeships, and worker reskilling, accompanied by an employer reskilling tax credit.
Implements measures to safeguard student and worker data privacy, including strict prohibitions on selling personally identifiable student data and mandatory 72-hour data breach reporting.

Establishes research and capacity-building programs, regional centers, and environmental transparency requirements regarding the energy and water consumption of artificial intelligence infrastructure and data centers.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts beyond the general authorization totals are not detailed for every individual sub-grant.
Exact criteria for how federal agencies will distribute grants beyond broad priority categories are left to future regulatory rulemaking.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Artificial Intelligence Education and Workforce Readiness Act of 2026 establishes a human-centered federal framework for artificial intelligence in education and the workforce. The bill sets up grant programs, interagency councils, and strategic planning initiatives to promote ethical artificial intelligence teaching and learning, support workforce reskilling and apprenticeships, protect data privacy, address environmental impacts of artificial intelligence infrastructure, and ensure equitable access for underserved communities.
summary_detail.significance: This legislation represents a comprehensive federal effort to manage the societal disruptions caused by artificial intelligence across education, labor, and the environment. By coupling large-scale investments in training and research with strict guardrails on data privacy, algorithmic bias, and human oversight, the bill attempts to balance technological advancement with worker protection and civil rights.
